newsitem.title: UK: NFC sells Lynx in 49 mln stg restructuring.
newsitem.headline: NFC sells Lynx in 49 mln stg restructuring.

text.p: British freight firm NFC Plc announced a further round of restructuring on Wednesday, with the sale of its Lynx express parcels service and other of non-core businesses.
The company said the sell-offs and rationalisation would bring in 207 million pounds ($337.9 million) of cash, although it would be spending 39 million pounds on the reorganisation.

The company said it would make an exceptional charge of 49 million pounds in results for the second half of this year for the reorganisation. But it would also book in an exceptional profit of 20 million pounds from the disposals.
The restructuring would dilute "earnings growth" this year but was expected to start boosting earnings next year, "with the full impact being felt in 1998/99," the company said.
The disposals comprise Lynx, the BRS car leasing business in Britain and the remaining U.S. and Canadian businesses belonging to its Pickford's removals division.
The company said it was reorganising the BRS truck rental and contract hire and engineering business and has closed its Exel Logistics Next Day Pallet network.
It was consolidating its European management in Britain, Ireland and mainland Europe.

In addition, the continental European logistics business was set for a major overhaul with further cost reductions, disposals and closures planned because of NFC's exposure to "extremely difficult trading conditions facing the local food distribution networks".
The company announced the moves with its half-year results. Pretax profits rose 12.9 percent to 50.1 million pounds for the six months to March 31, on flat turnover of just over 1.17 billion pounds.
The interim dividend was maintained at 2.5 pence a share on earnings up 0.4 pence at 4.3 pence.
